findings.reason: the node is sent to make review completions answer `already_promoted` in `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py`, but the behaviour it must change lives in `promotion.py`, outside §17's declared write paths, so the section as written can only end "blocked" (as its own hedge anticipates).
findings.text: §17 asserts "A second completion of a run that is already promoted does not answer `already_promoted`, as it does for an implement run, but re-runs its landing writes", but `already_promoted` is computed identically for every run role in the shared path `reckon/crew/promotion.py::_complete_locked` (set at `promotion.py:1103` on the existing-row branch and at `:1590` on the append-collision branch), and neither branch returns before `_commit_landing_writes` — so a second completion of an implement run re-runs its landing writes too, and the role contrast the section draws does not exist. The incident's own `landing.json` for `r-20261020T082557577198-...` has the per-run ledger file in the rollback map, which is the append branch's path list (`promotion.py:1676`, the ledger path first), not the existing-row branch's comment-only list (`:1667`); so the second completion reached the append branch because the row was not read back, and the defect is the missing short-circuit, not a review-run-specific behaviour.

findings.reason: with one verdict covering both, a node that lands the retry and stops blocked on the idempotence half cannot be closed on either.
findings.text: §17's deliverable states two independent behaviours — "The landing staging retries a failure whose message names a held `index.lock` ... before refusing" and "A `crew complete` of a run whose ledger row and promote commit already exist answers `already_promoted` without rewriting its records" — and the done-when carries a separate verdict for each, so one node's gate proves neither wholly; the plan itself concedes the second may "belong elsewhere".

findings.reason: a control that does not cover half the done-when lets that half pass on the unfixed code, which is the exact failure the control exists to prevent.
findings.text: the declared negative control ("removes the retry, and the first case then refuses") exercises only the staging-retry half; the second half's requirement that a second completion "answers `already_promoted` and leaves its committed record untouched" has no inverse case, so an implementation that re-runs the landing writes on a second completion would still satisfy every declared assertion.

findings.reason: the fleet delivery contract already pins a node's logs under its run directory, so the omission is redundant with a binding rule rather than a wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §17 states its suite and lint logs must "start with [their] revision and the literal command and end in `EXIT=`" but, unlike §14/§15/§16, names no directory for them, so the gate logs a later reader must open have no declared durable path.
